column4: Paradise contains سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ, raised couches; immediately before cups are “placed” in 88:14, this restages the section's elevation and placement as a furnished interior.
وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ names cups deliberately placed beside the raised couches of 88:13, an exact small-scale pairing of وضع and رفع.
Cushions are arrayed in rows after the raised couches and placed cups; this contributes ordered arrangement to the same paradisal construction scene.
Carpets are spread out after 88:13–15, completing the arranged floor beneath the elevated and placed furnishings.
سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى commands the prophetic addressee to glorify the name of his Most High Lord, bringing raised name, Lord, and directed worship into one line.
Immediately after asking for chest-opening and a loosened knot, Moses asks his Lord for a وَزِيرًا from his family; the helper stands against a solitary bearer crushed by his load.
Moses asks ٱشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِى, “strengthen my back through him”; this directly reverses the section's back weakened to the point of creaking under a burden.
وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى gives the purpose of the strengthened back in 20:31: the entrusted affair will be shared rather than borne alone.
God gives Moses the Book and makes his brother Aaron a وَزِيرًا with him, supplying the divinely granted helper associated with bearing and supporting a weighty task.
God promises Moses سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ, strengthening his arm through his brother; bodily support counters the image of a body failing beneath its work.
God opens a person's chest to submission, but makes another chest tight and constricted كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ; chest-opening and difficult upward motion meet in a single contrast.
One whose chest God has opened to submission stands in light from his Lord, an explicit parallel to the divinely opened chest in the surah.
مَن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا uses an opened chest for willing unbelief; it is the moral reversal that shows chest-opening is not automatically relief or guidance.
The Prophet is told not to let there be حَرَجٌ in his chest because of the revealed Book, another divine address relieving prophetic constriction.
The possibility that the Prophet's chest becomes constricted by objections to revelation supplies a specific pressure from which divine chest-opening relieves him.
Moses says his chest constricts and his tongue does not proceed freely; this joins the two impairments answered by the prayer of 20:25–27.

Dhu al-Qarnayn asks the people to help him بِقُوَّةٍ so he may make a barrier between them and their enemies; this states the cooperative force and protective purpose behind the construction in 18:96.
A mosque founded عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ supplies the stable foundation against which 9:109's collapsing building is judged.
Their building remains a doubt in their hearts إِلَّآ أَن تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ; the built structure persists until the builders' own inner bodies are cut apart.
Those who take a mosque for harm and division make a religious building serve rupture; 9:108–109 answer it with foundations of reverence and a collapsing bank.
The spider's house is called أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ, the frailest of houses; it is a built form whose weakness makes misplaced reliance visible.
The heavens and earth were رَتْقًا, sewn or closed together, before God فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا, split them apart; creation itself begins with the opening of a joined structure.
The sky and earth تَقُومَانِ بِأَمْرِهِ, stand by God's command; cosmic stability is expressed as sustained uprightness.
The earth and mountains are carried and crushed in one blow; raised and anchored creation becomes a borne mass that is structurally demolished.
When the earth is shaken violently, the stable ground of the construction image begins to come apart; 56:5–6 give the mountains' resulting dissolution.
وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسًّا says the mountains are pulverized, directly reversing their installation as firm pegs.
The pulverized mountains become scattered dust, completing the dismantling begun in 56:4–5.
God will roll up the sky كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ; the raised canopy is deliberately folded away like a written scroll.
The earth is wholly in God's grasp and the heavens are folded in His right hand, a final reversal of the spread earth and raised sky.
إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ repeats the Quran's direct image of the built heaven splitting open.
إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ gives another explicit dissolution of the raised sky and immediately places it under obedience to its Lord.
When the sky splits and becomes rose-red like oil or hide, the ordered heaven raised in 55:7 reaches its eschatological undoing in the same surah.
When the sky is fissured, the elevated cosmic structure passes from integrity to opening.
وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ depicts the sky stripped away, a different mode of dismantling the overhead structure.
The sky is split open with clouds and angels descend, presenting a breach in the raised canopy rather than its stable elevation.
God spreads the earth and casts firm mountains into it; horizontal preparation and installed masses repeat the section's construction grammar.
God casts firm mountains into earth lest it sway with people, giving the erected forms a stabilizing structural function.
Firm mountains are placed in the earth so it will not shake with its inhabitants, another explicit act of stabilizing installation.
God places firm mountains above the earth and apportions its provisions, joining installed structure to measured provision.
The earth is spread and firm mountains are cast into it, recreating the laid plane and erected forms of the section's central tableau.
وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَرْسَىٰهَا anchors the mountains after the earth is spread, giving structural fixation to the creation sequence begun with the raised sky.
God extends the earth and makes in it firm mountains, another direct pairing of horizontal expanse and fixed elevation.
God places lofty firm mountains on earth and gives sweet water, connecting raised mass with provision from the prepared world.
Destroyed settlements lie خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا, fallen upon their roofs, beside an abandoned well and lofty palace; built height and ruin share one landscape.
Believers receive chambers with further chambers built above them, a literal structure articulated through vertical layering.
إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ identifies Iram by its pillars, placing monumental upright supports in the passage that later names Pharaoh's stakes.
Thamud carve rock in the valley, turning the mountain material itself into durable human construction.
Thamud carve houses from mountains after being settled in the land; erected dwelling is cut directly out of a fixed natural mass.
They carve houses from mountains while feeling secure, making architectural firmness the setting for a security that proves temporary.
Thamud carve skillful houses from mountains, another repeated scene of shaping the massive erected form into built shelter.

The people command one another to build a structure for Abraham and cast him into its fire; human construction is turned into an instrument of destruction against the future raiser of the House's foundations.
God makes the House a recurring destination and security and names Abraham's station as a place of prayer; it clarifies the placed House as an appointed human locus.
God sends down the Book with truth and the balance, paralleling 55:7's placed measure and tying cosmic order to revealed judgment.
The people within the raised houses of 24:36 are not distracted from God's remembrance and prayer; this supplies the enacted dhikr for which those houses are elevated.
The Prophet is told to glorify God during the night and at the retreat of the stars, continuing 52:48's command to praise his Lord when he rises.
The night worshipper is prostrate and standing, wary of the hereafter and hoping for his Lord's mercy; upright exertion is explicitly directed by fear and desire toward the Lord.
Servants of the Merciful spend the night لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا, prostrate and standing for their Lord, enacting the posture and direction of the final commands.
وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands remembrance of the Lord's name morning and evening; 76:26 then gives its bodily worship forms.
Night prostration and prolonged glorification enact the exertion commanded after remembering the Lord's name in 76:25.
وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب commands prostration and approach, another concise bodily orientation toward the Lord after opposition.
مَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ reverses the section's رغبة “toward” the Lord by using the same stance “away from” Abraham's way; Abraham is also the builder in 2:127.
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ addresses the human as laboring toward his Lord, joining exertion and directed movement exactly as the section's last two commands do.
وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ states that the final end is toward the Lord, grounding the directional force of إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ.
إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ makes return to the Lord the endpoint, another concise statement of the section's final orientation.
رَفِيعُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتِ describes God as exalted in degrees or raiser of ranks, extending the elevation field from structures and servants to the Lord's own majesty.
The honored pages are مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ, raised and purified; elevation marks the rank of revelation rather than the position of a building.
وَفُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ adds raised couches or beds to the Quran's furnished scenes, paralleling the raised couches of 88:13.
Those who lower their voices before God's messenger are praised, completing 49:2's prohibition and setting human self-lowering beside God's elevation of the Prophet's remembrance.
وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ says God left Noah an enduring mention among later people, a concrete form of preserved and elevated remembrance.
God leaves Abraham's mention among later generations, directly answering Abraham's request in 26:84 for truthful later renown.
God leaves Moses and Aaron an enduring mention among later people, repeating the form of divinely preserved reputation.
God leaves Elias an enduring mention among later people, another repeated realization of remembrance carried beyond a prophet's lifetime.
The revealed Book contains ذِكْرُكُمْ, which can mean the audience's reminder or honor; this is a plausible communal counterpart to an elevated personal dhikr.
God and His angels bless the Prophet and believers are commanded to bless him, providing an enacted, continually repeated form of his elevated remembrance.
Palms are either cut down or left قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا, standing on their roots; the ayah explicitly places severed and upright forms across one boundary.
People are torn away like trunks of uprooted palms, turning an upright living form into a bodily image of removal from its base.
Abraham makes the idols جُذَٰذًا, shattered pieces, except their largest; objects of cultic erection are physically dismantled.
Abraham turns upon the idols, striking them with his right hand, another concrete undoing of standing cult objects.
When the plague is removed until an appointed term, Pharaoh's people immediately يَنكُثُونَ, undoing their promise like a loosened bond.
After punishment is removed from them, إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ; relief is answered by breaking the pledged response.
The burden carried in 20:100 persists, and the ayah calls it an evil load on resurrection; it supplies the crushing duration and valuation of that burden.
God forms bones, clothes them with flesh, and produces another creation; the body is assembled stage by stage rather than allowed to come apart.
The objector presents decayed bones and asks who can revive them, posing bodily disassembly as a challenge answered in 36:79.
God who produced the bones the first time will revive them, establishing divine reconstruction after complete bodily decay.
The fire closes over them فِى عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ, in extended columns; this may recall erected supports, though the image's exact spatial arrangement is uncertain.
